tools.name: add_scripts_to_plan
tools.description: Put finished scripts into the user's Daily Studio content plan, each with the day it should go out. Use this when the user asks you to PLAN — a week, a month, a series — rather than to hand them something to record right now. The plan lives on their account: it shows up in the app, on dailystudio.ap

tools.name: list_planned_scripts
tools.description: Read what is already in the user's Daily Studio content plan — each script's id, title, collection, the day it goes out, its place in the shoot order, and how far it has got (written, recorded, uploaded, scheduled, published, or failed). tools.name: edit_planned_scripts
tools.description: Change scripts already in the user's Daily Studio content plan, by id and in bulk: move them to other days, group them into collections, retitle or rewrite them. This is the tool for 'these contents go on these days, grouped like this' when the content already exists — read the plan first with list_

tools.name: get_planned_scripts
tools.description: Read the full text of specific scripts in the user's content plan, by id — the words themselves, not just titles. Use it before rewriting or reviewing a script, or when the user asks about one ('check the hook on Tuesday's'). Up to 20 per call.

tools.name: archive_planned_scripts
tools.description: Archive scripts out of the user's working plan, by id — or restore archived ones with `restore: true`. tools.name: reorder_planned_scripts
tools.description: Set the order the user's camera walks through their scripts — pass ids first-to-record first. Scripts you leave out keep their current order after the ones you name. Use it when the user says what to shoot first, or after planning a batch that should be recorded in sequence.

tools.name: list_collections
tools.description: List the collections (piles) the user already groups their scripts into, with counts. Call it before grouping anything so you reuse their existing names instead of inventing near-duplicates.

tools.name: list_scheduled_posts
tools.description: Read what the user has approved for publishing and what happened to it: waiting, going up now, published (with the link), failed (with the reason in plain words), or cancelled. Call it when the user asks 'did my post go out?' or 'why not?'. Nothing is changed by this tool, and new posts cannot be sc

tools.name: cancel_scheduled_post
tools.description: Cancel one post that is waiting to go out, by id from list_scheduled_posts. Only works while the post is still waiting; the take becomes approvable again. Confirm with the user before calling this — it withdraws something they approved.

tools.name: retry_scheduled_post
tools.description: Put one failed post back in the queue, due now — by id from list_scheduled_posts. Use it after the cause in the failure sentence is fixed (say, a reconnected account). The post goes out within about five minutes.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "cancel_scheduled_post" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Cancel one post that is waiting to go out, by id from list_scheduled_posts. Only works while the post is still waiting; the take becomes approvable again. Confi…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_scheduled_posts · Private data: send_script_to_teleprompter, add_scripts_to_plan, reorder_planned_scripts · Public sink: send_script_to_teleprompter, edit_planned_scripts, list_scheduled_posts, cancel_scheduled_post, retry_scheduled_post.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_scheduled_posts · Private data: send_script_to_teleprompter, add_scripts_to_plan, reorder_planned_scripts · Public sink: send_script_to_teleprompter, edit_planned_scripts, list_scheduled_posts, cancel_scheduled_post, retry_scheduled_post

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
